St Mary's C E Primary School - Christian Distinctiveness
pageCache.text:
Christian Distinctiveness
St Mary’s Church of England Primary School is extremely proud to be part of a wider family of 155 church schools belonging to the well-established Diocese of London. Our staff, Advisory Board and our Church Partner St Mary’s Willesden are committed to ensuring the best possible educational experience for every child in our care, regardless of whether they come from a Christian background, a different religious background, or a background of no religion at all.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's C E Primary School - Our Church School
pageCache.text:
Our Church School
At St Mary’s C E Primary School, we are proud of the distinctive Christian ethos that permeates every aspect of school life. Guided by our vision — “Live, Love and Learn Together in the Light of the Life of Christ” — we seek to ensure that every member of our school community flourishes in mind, body, heart, and spirit.
Our vision is theologically rooted in Ephesians 5:8–11, 13–14:
“For once you were in darkness, but now in the Lord you are light. Live as children of light.”
This verse inspires us to nurture children who live as lights in the world — kind, compassionate, and confident individuals who reflect God’s love in all they do. Our core Christian values of Faith, Hope, and Charity shape our relationships, decision-making, and collective worship, helping pupils grow in character and wisdom.
We encourage all in our community to Be Respectful, Be Responsible, and Be Ready to Learn, ensuring that our actions and attitudes reflect our shared commitment to living as children of light.
Through the teaching of Religious Education, we help pupils develop the knowledge, empathy, and critical thinking skills needed to hold balanced and well-informed conversations about religion and worldviews, and to form their own reflective, personal worldview.
St Mary’s is often described as having a true ‘family feel’ — a place where staff model Christian values in all they do, and pupils are recognised for their warmth, courtesy, and care for others.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's C E Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to St Mary’s CE Primary School.
It is a great privilege and honour to welcome you to our wonderful school as Headteacher. Having been a teacher at St Mary’s for the past 11 years, and serving as Deputy Headteacher for the last three years, I am incredibly proud to lead a school and community that I know so well and care deeply about.
At the heart of everything we do is our school vision: "To Live, Love and Learn Together in the Light of the Life of Christ." This vision guides and inspires our whole school community. We strive to follow the example of Christ in the way we treat one another; with kindness, compassion, respect and forgiveness, ensuring that every child feels valued, supported and encouraged to be the very best version of themselves.
We believe that children thrive when they feel safe, loved and inspired to learn. Our dedicated staff work hard to provide an engaging and ambitious curriculum that enables all pupils to achieve their full potential academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually. We encourage our children to embrace challenges, develop resilience and become confident, caring individuals who make a positive contribution to the world around them.
St Mary’s is a school built on strong partnerships between home, school, church and the wider community. Together, we create an environment where everyone belongs and where our shared values shape our daily lives. We are proud of our inclusive and nurturing ethos, which helps every child to flourish and grow.
Whether you are already part of our school family or considering St Mary’s for your child, I hope our website provides a glimpse into the warmth, commitment and sense of community that make our school such a special place. We would be delighted to welcome you and share more about all that St Mary’s has to offer.
I look forward to working together as we continue to build on the many successes of our school and ensure that every child has the opportunity to live, love and learn together in the light of the life of Christ.
Mrs Rochelle Sylvester

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's C E Primary School - Safeguarding
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
For any matters concerning safeguarding, please email the school's DSL, Mrs Rochelle Sylvester, on: safeguarding@stmarysce.brent.sch.uk
At St Mary’s, keeping you safe is the most important thing we do. We want every child to feel happy, healthy and safe and able to talk to adults if something is worrying them.
You can always speak to any trusted adult in school: teachers, support staff, the office team or the safeguarding leads. We will listen to you, take you seriously and help you get the support you need.
We work with organisations like the NSPCC, who help schools understand how to keep children safe and teach you how to speak up if something doesn’t feel right. Their advice helps us make sure our school is a safe place for everyone.
We also work together with your families and other professionals to make sure you are safe at home, in school and online. Your voice matters, and your thoughts and feelings help us make good decisions.
If you ever feel unsafe, worried or unsure about something, please talk to an adult you trust. You can also contact Childline on 0800 1111 — “Whatever your worry, they’re here to help.”
At St Mary’s, you are valued, you are listened to, and you deserve to feel safe every day.
soss participation certificate stmceps.pdf
Safeguarding our children
We want your children to be healthy and happy … and to develop well both physically and mentally. Children learn through exploration and natural curiosity, and it is part of our job as teachers and your job as parents to encourage that. However, as your children grow up, develop and discover new experiences, we have to take more and different steps to ensure their safety.
Until their understanding and instincts catch up with their curiosity, your children need to be protected from everyday dangers – whether crossing the road, in and around the home and school, trying new foods or talking to new people they meet.
And sooner or later … going online.
They’re growing up fast
But they almost certainly don’t have the life-experience and wisdom to handle all of the situations they encounter. Chances are, they know more about these things than you do. Depending on the age that your children are now, they may not have yet discovered computers, smartphones or tablets, unless it’s just pressing the buttons! Alternatively, they may already be used to using certain trusted websites and apps or – if they’re older – using social networking sites.
The risks
None of us – of whatever age – is immune from encountering problems online, as a look through the daily news will tell you. Your children are certainly at a vulnerable stage in their lives … naturally more trusting than adults and hopefully having been less exposed to the darker side of the internet. They are also not as well equipped to deal with such issues – or their consequences.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's C E Primary School - Outdoor Learning and Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning and Curriculum
At St Mary’s Primary, we value outdoor learning as a vital part of our curriculum, connecting children directly with nature and the world around them. Through the Our Schools, Our World programme and our focus on greening the curriculum, we nurture young people as informed and responsible global citizens—ecologically, economically, culturally, and spiritually.
Our outdoor and greening initiatives enable students to learn effectively about sustainability, climate change, biodiversity, and other environmental issues, embedding ecological awareness across subjects. Children develop the knowledge, skills, and creativity needed to address local and global challenges, and are encouraged to see themselves as changemakers—taking part in initiatives that foster hope and positive action for the planet, while observing their schools as sustainable, socially engaged communities.
By engaging regularly with nature and experiencing a curriculum that integrates environmental learning across subjects, students at St Mary’s develop a deep connection to the natural world, a sense of responsibility, and the confidence to influence their wider communities. Outdoor learning and the greening of the curriculum inspire, inform, and motivate pupils to make meaningful contributions to a sustainable future.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's C E Primary School - Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
pageCache.text:
Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
At St Mary’s, we believe that every child is wonderfully made and deeply valued. Guided by our Christian vision and our calling to live as Children of Light — shining with love, respect and justice — we are committed to creating a school community where everyone feels safe, included and celebrated for who they are.
We strive to ensure that equality, diversity and inclusion are at the heart of everything we do — from our curriculum and worship to our relationships and wider school life. Our aim is for every pupil to know that they belong, to recognise their own worth, and to develop as compassionate global citizens who value difference and challenge injustice.
Together, we learn to live out The St Mary’s Way – being Respectful, Responsible and Ready to Learn – so that all can flourish and achieve their God-given potential.
